344|## 4. Agent loop (`anamnesis/agent/`, batches 14 and 15.5)
345|`run_intake(audio, images, ...)` runs a **fixed order**; no model chooses actions, nothing a model wrote is surfaced except source data (transcripts, label text), and there are no outer retries (adapters retry once themselves).
346|0. **Prepare** every photo before any model sees it (`prepare_image(data, mime) -> (data, mime)`, `anamnesis/agent/media.py`). Phones store the pixels sideways and record the turn in EXIF; SAM applies it and Spark does not (live, 27 Oct: on a portrait photo, 2 of 3 labels were read from the wrong pack). Preparation turns the pixels upright for every EXIF orientation (1–8) and drops all metadata (EXIF including GPS and camera tags, XMP, IPTC, ICC profiles, comments, PNG text chunks, and any extra frames such as an HDR gain map), so SAM, Spark, the crop and the brief see the same pixels and no location leaves the machine. A JPEG or PNG that is already upright and carries none of these is returned byte for byte. Otherwise a JPEG (including a multi-picture MPO, primary frame only) is re-encoded as JPEG (quality 95, 4:4:4 chroma), and anything else as PNG. Preparation is deterministic and idempotent; region hashes and `intake_id` use the prepared bytes, and callers that show a photo (the brief) show the prepared bytes. Bytes that can't be decoded raise `ValueError`; the loop then logs one `segment` step `error: image cannot be decoded` with no call ids, sends that photo to no model, and goes on with the next.
347|1. `transcribe` if there is audio. 2. `extract_claims` if there are turns.
348|3. Per image, `segment` with each concept in order (`medicine box`, `label`, `package`), stopping at the first that returns a region. `package` came in batch 23: on 28 Oct SAM 3.1 found no region with the first two in 19 of 30 Cairo University phone photos, `package` found one in all 19, and Spark 1.3 read 15 of those crops right (`evidence/batches/22/comparison.md`).
349|4. **Read the crop first (Z8, batch 18).** For each of the `top_regions(k=3)` of each image: only regions whose `image_sha256` and frame size match the prepared photo are kept, ranked and published in the report; each other region gets one `read` step `error: region does not match the photo` and is dropped. Each kept region is cut with `crop_region` (padded by 5% of the box size on each side, i.e. 10% in total, rounded down and clamped to the frame; refused unless the sha256 and frame size match the region) and the reader is called on the **crop only**, as PNG, with `cropped=True`. The reader never sees the full photo, so a reading can only describe the pixels of its own region (provenance by construction; live, 27 Oct: 8/8 crop reads correct at 465–1,001 input tokens against about 4,300 for the full photo). A crop that fails logs one `read` step `error: crop failed` (no provider call) and the region gets no reading. Once the session is exhausted, no crop is cut and nothing is logged.
350|5. Each `unreadable` or `partial` reading gets **one** `zoom_read`: the same crop, upscaled 2× (Lanczos; the factor is lowered so the longest side is at most 2,048 px; if that factor is ≤ 1 there is no zoom and no step), read with `cropped=True`. The new reading keeps the **source** `region_id`, so provenance stays in source pixels. SAM never runs on a crop. At most 2 reads per region (`max_grounding_iters = 2`). Both the read and the zoom cut their crop through the name `crop_region` in `anamnesis/agent/loop.py`.

457|- its heading, an `<h3>`: the first non-blank line of the claim's `name_text`, otherwise of the label text, otherwise "Unnamed pack";
458|- `TEMPLATES[type]`, and the patient question when there is one;
459|- the two sides **side by side**: `data-side="patient"` (name, the scalar `inn` when there is one, strength and intake amount with each ingredient's salt, regimen and status, verbatim) and `data-side="pack"` (label text, the scalar `inn` when there is one, strength with each ingredient's salt, readability, country). A salt-only `formulation_mismatch` must show both salts, wherever rule 6 found them, including a salt named only in `name_text` or the label text (QM M4 code #5 and round 2 #1; supervisor 19.1 #3). The Name, Ingredient and Label text rows are HTML-escaped and marked `dir="auto"` (supervisor 19.1 round 2; batch 21). On both sides, each amount and its unit is wrapped in `<bdi dir="ltr">`, so an Arabic row reads "50 mg", never "mg 50" (judge-facing session, 28 Oct; batch 21). Amounts print as plain decimals with their unit and never with a trailing zero ("100 mg", never "100.0 mg"; "0.5", never ".5"), the safe-notation rule for doses. A missing side says "Not mentioned." or "Not photographed.";
460|- **Catalogue codes (batch 24.1).**
461|  - **Which box shows them:** a finding box whose claim's `name_text` resolves to a catalogue entry with codes, or, when there is no claim, whose pack's `label_text` does.
462|  - **What it shows:** one line under the two sides, `Catalogue codes: ATC … · RxNorm …`, with only the codes the entry has. Codes are escaped, and there's no link.
463|  - **The reference line:** once per page, when any code is shown. It names the WHO Collaborating Centre for Drug Statistics Methodology and points to `NOTICE`. It never names NLM, whose terms ask apps not to use its name.
464|  - **No codes beside a contradiction (batch 24.2):** a box shows no codes line when its side contradicts its own name. That uses the reconciler's own identity check: the claim's name against its stated INN and strength, or the pack's label against its strength, with the pack's country. A code says which medicine a name is, so when the patient's own words or the pack's own reading dispute the name, the brief shows no code rather than a disputed one. The batch 24.1 supervisor found the case: "Concor" said with "atorvastatin" showed bisoprolol's codes.
465|- A3 wording: a `missing_modality` finding is labelled "Mentioned, not photographed" or "Photographed, not mentioned", and one in `stopped` "Reported as stopped, not photographed";
466|- a link to every piece of its evidence: `href="#turn:<turn_id>"` for each audio turn, `href="#region:<region_id>"` for each region.

468|**Evidence on the page.**
469|- Each photo that opens is `<figure id="photo:<i>">` (input order, from 1), with one `<img>` of the **prepared** bytes (§4 step 0) under an `<svg viewBox="0 0 <frame_w> <frame_h>">`. The svg has one `<rect>` per report region of that photo, at `x1, y1`, `x2 − x1 + 1` wide and `y2 − y1 + 1` high, inside `<a href="#region:<region_id>">`. A box is an outline with a transparent fill, so the pack under it stays visible and the whole box is clickable. No image makes the page wider than the screen.
470|- Each report region is `<figure id="region:<region_id>">` showing `crop_region(prepared photo, region)`. For a region that was read, these are exactly the pixels of the reader's first read (a `zoom_read` saw the same crop enlarged 2×); this is the click-to-zoom view. A report region whose photo isn't among the given photos is refused with `ValueError`, never skipped.
471|- The voice note is one `<audio src="data:…">`. Each turn is `<li id="turn:<turn_id>" data-start-ms="…" data-end-ms="…">` with its time range and transcript. Clicking it plays that turn only, from its start to its end, and starting another turn ends the first. The contract runs the script in Node against a small DOM, so the script uses only `querySelector`/`querySelectorAll` with tag and attribute selectors, `getElementById`, `getAttribute`, `dataset`, `closest` and `addEventListener`.

Pairwise reconciliation can't see two medicines that overlap each other: the showcase patient reports Concor and Beloc-Zok, two beta-blockers. Only **claims** count, never the photos, because a pack can't show use and repeated photos never imply duplicate use.

65|    session: IntakeSession, segmenter, reader, prepared: Prepared, concepts: tuple[str, ...], top_k: int,
66|) -> tuple[list[ImageRegion], list[tuple[Image, ImageRegion, LabelReading]]]:
67|    """Segment one photo, keep the regions that belong to it, read the best ones, log the rest as dropped."""
68|    image, size, sha = prepared

70|    kept = [r for r in found if r.image_sha256 == sha and (r.frame_w, r.frame_h) == size]
71|    for region in found:

73|            session.note(AgentAction.READ, region.region_id, "error: region does not match the photo")
74|    readings = []

95|) -> LabelReading:
96|    """One crop-zoom re-read of the source region; keeps the source region id."""
97|    if session.exhausted:  # budget_exhausted is the last step: no crop, no log
98|        return reading
99|    try:
100|        crop = crop_region(image[0], region)
101|    except ValueError:
102|        session.note(AgentAction.ZOOM_READ, region.region_id, "error: crop failed")
103|        return reading
104|    enlarged = enlarge_crop(crop)
105|    if enlarged is None:  # already at the size cap: no zoom, no step, no call
106|        return reading
107|    zoomed = session.call(

110|        lambda new: new.readability.value,

130|    catalogue: Catalogue, language_bias: list[str] | None = None, keywords: list[str] | None = None,
131|    lang_hint: str | None = None, concepts: tuple[str, ...] = SAM_CONCEPTS,
132|    top_k: int = 3, max_provider_calls: int | None = None,
133|) -> ReconciliationReport:
134|    """Run one patient intake in a fixed order and return the single report artifact."""
135|    if max_provider_calls is None:
136|        max_provider_calls = 2 + (len(concepts) + 2 * top_k) * len(images)
137|    session = IntakeSession(max_provider_calls)
138|    turns = []

143|                audio, language_bias=language_bias, keywords=keywords, lang_hint=lang_hint),
144|            lambda found: f"{len(found)} turns",
145|        ) or []
146|    claims = []

150|            lambda found: f"{len(found)} claims",

172|def voice(path: Path) -> bytes:
173|    """The WAV's audio frames alone, re-written so no metadata chunk reaches a model or a brief (M8 #7)."""
174|    try:
175|        with wave.open(io.BytesIO(path.read_bytes())) as source:
176|            params, frames = source.getparams(), source.readframes(source.getnframes())
177|    except (wave.Error, EOFError) as exc:
178|        sys.exit(f"{path}: not a PCM WAV ({exc}); convert it with ffmpeg -map_metadata -1 first")
179|    out = io.BytesIO()
180|    with wave.open(out, "wb") as clean:
181|        clean.setparams(params)
182|        clean.writeframes(frames)
183|    return out.getvalue()

1|"""Call budget, spend and step log for one intake. The only mutable state in the loop."""
2|
3|from collections.abc import Callable
4|from decimal import Decimal
5|from typing import Any
6|
7|from anamnesis.providers.base import ProviderError, ProviderTrace
8|from anamnesis.providers.spend import SpendCapExceeded
9|from anamnesis.schema.report import AgentAction, AgentStep

11|
12|def _error_outcome(exc: Exception) -> str:
13|    """Describe an error without any provider or model prose."""
14|    if isinstance(exc, ProviderError):
15|        return f"error: {exc.provider} {type(exc).__name__}"
16|    return f"error: {type(exc).__name__}"
17|
18|
19|def _attempt_fields(attempt: ProviderTrace | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
20|    if attempt is None:
21|        return {}
22|    return {"model_id": attempt.model_id, "input_tokens": attempt.input_tokens,
23|            "output_tokens": attempt.output_tokens, "latency_ms": attempt.latency_ms}
24|
25|
26|class IntakeSession:
27|    """Counts provider calls against a budget and records one step per action."""
28|
29|    def __init__(self, max_provider_calls: int) -> None:
30|        self.max_provider_calls = max_provider_calls
31|        self.calls = 0
32|        self.spend_usd = Decimal(0)
33|        self.exhausted = False
34|        self.steps: list[AgentStep] = []
35|
36|    def note(self, action: AgentAction, target: str, outcome: str, call_ids: list[str] | None = None,
37|             model_id: str | None = None, input_tokens: int = 0, output_tokens: int = 0,
38|             latency_ms: int = 0, cost_usd: Decimal = Decimal(0)) -> None:
39|        self.steps.append(AgentStep(n=len(self.steps), action=action, target=target, outcome=outcome,
40|                                    call_ids=call_ids or [], model_id=model_id, input_tokens=input_tokens,
41|                                    output_tokens=output_tokens, latency_ms=latency_ms, cost_usd=cost_usd))
42|
43|    def call(self, action: AgentAction, target: str, fn: Callable[[], tuple[Any, ProviderTrace | None]],
44|             describe: Callable[[Any], str]) -> Any | None:
45|        """Run one provider call within budget. Returns its value, or None if skipped or failed."""
46|        if self.exhausted or self.calls >= self.max_provider_calls:
47|            if not self.exhausted:
48|                self.exhausted = True
49|                self.note(AgentAction.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, action.value,
50|                          f"max_provider_calls={self.max_provider_calls}")
51|            return None
52|        self.calls += 1
53|        try:
54|            value, trace = fn()
55|        except SpendCapExceeded as exc:  # a money cap ends the session, like the call budget
56|            self.exhausted = True
57|            self.spend_usd += exc.charged_usd  # attempts charged before the cap refused the next one
58|            attempt = getattr(exc, "attempt_trace", None)
59|            self.note(AgentAction.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, target, _error_outcome(exc), exc.charged_call_ids,
60|                      **_attempt_fields(attempt), cost_usd=exc.charged_usd)
61|            return None
62|        except ProviderError as exc:  # charged attempts of a failed call still count as spend
63|            self.spend_usd += exc.charged_usd
64|            self.note(action, target, _error_outcome(exc), exc.charged_call_ids,
65|                      **_attempt_fields(exc.attempt_trace), cost_usd=exc.charged_usd)
66|            return None
67|        except ValueError as exc:  # a non-provider error may still follow charged attempts
68|            charged = getattr(exc, "charged_usd", Decimal(0))
69|            self.spend_usd += charged
70|            self.note(action, target, _error_outcome(exc), getattr(exc, "charged_call_ids", []),
71|                      **_attempt_fields(getattr(exc, "attempt_trace", None)), cost_usd=charged)
72|            return None
73|        ids = self._charge(trace)
74|        if trace is None:
75|            self.note(action, target, describe(value), ids)
76|        else:
77|            self.note(action, target, describe(value), ids, model_id=trace.model_id,
78|                      input_tokens=trace.input_tokens, output_tokens=trace.output_tokens,
79|                      latency_ms=trace.latency_ms, cost_usd=trace.cost_usd + trace.prior_cost_usd)
80|        return value
81|
82|    def _charge(self, trace: ProviderTrace | None) -> list[str]:
83|        if trace is None:
84|            return []
85|        self.spend_usd += trace.cost_usd + trace.prior_cost_usd
86|        return [trace.call_id, *trace.prior_call_ids]

1|"""Call budget, spend and step log for one intake. The only mutable state in the loop."""
2|
3|from collections.abc import Callable
4|from decimal import Decimal
5|from typing import Any
6|
7|from anamnesis.providers.base import ProviderError, ProviderTrace
8|from anamnesis.providers.spend import SpendCapExceeded
9|from anamnesis.schema.report import AgentAction, AgentStep
10|
11|
12|def _error_outcome(exc: Exception) -> str:
13|    """Describe an error without any provider or model prose."""
14|    if isinstance(exc, ProviderError):
15|        return f"error: {exc.provider} {type(exc).__name__}"
16|    return f"error: {type(exc).__name__}"
17|
18|
19|def _attempt_fields(attempt: ProviderTrace | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
20|    if attempt is None:
21|        return {}
22|    return {"model_id": attempt.model_id, "input_tokens": attempt.input_tokens,
23|            "output_tokens": attempt.output_tokens, "latency_ms": attempt.latency_ms}
24|
25|
26|class IntakeSession:
27|    """Counts provider calls against a budget and records one step per action."""
28|
29|    def __init__(self, max_provider_calls: int) -> None:
30|        self.max_provider_calls = max_provider_calls
31|        self.calls = 0
32|        self.spend_usd = Decimal(0)
33|        self.exhausted = False
34|        self.steps: list[AgentStep] = []
35|
36|    def note(self, action: AgentAction, target: str, outcome: str, call_ids: list[str] | None = None,
37|             model_id: str | None = None, input_tokens: int = 0, output_tokens: int = 0,
38|             latency_ms: int = 0, cost_usd: Decimal = Decimal(0)) -> None:
39|        self.steps.append(AgentStep(n=len(self.steps), action=action, target=target, outcome=outcome,
40|                                    call_ids=call_ids or [], model_id=model_id, input_tokens=input_tokens,
41|                                    output_tokens=output_tokens, latency_ms=latency_ms, cost_usd=cost_usd))
42|
43|    def call(self, action: AgentAction, target: str, fn: Callable[[], tuple[Any, ProviderTrace | None]],
44|             describe: Callable[[Any], str]) -> Any | None:
45|        """Run one provider call within budget. Returns its value, or None if skipped or failed."""
46|        if self.exhausted or self.calls >= self.max_provider_calls:
47|            if not self.exhausted:
48|                self.exhausted = True
49|                self.note(AgentAction.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, action.value,
50|                          f"max_provider_calls={self.max_provider_calls}")
51|            return None
52|        self.calls += 1
53|        try:
54|            value, trace = fn()
55|        except SpendCapExceeded as exc:  # a money cap ends the session, like the call budget
56|            self.exhausted = True
57|            self.spend_usd += exc.charged_usd  # attempts charged before the cap refused the next one
58|            attempt = getattr(exc, "attempt_trace", None)
59|            self.note(AgentAction.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, target, _error_outcome(exc), exc.charged_call_ids,
60|                      **_attempt_fields(attempt), cost_usd=exc.charged_usd)
61|            return None
62|        except ProviderError as exc:  # charged attempts of a failed call still count as spend
63|            self.spend_usd += exc.charged_usd
64|            self.note(action, target, _error_outcome(exc), exc.charged_call_ids,
65|                      **_attempt_fields(exc.attempt_trace), cost_usd=exc.charged_usd)
66|            return None
67|        except ValueError as exc:  # a non-provider error may still follow charged attempts
68|            charged = getattr(exc, "charged_usd", Decimal(0))
69|            self.spend_usd += charged
70|            self.note(action, target, _error_outcome(exc), getattr(exc, "charged_call_ids", []),
71|                      **_attempt_fields(getattr(exc, "attempt_trace", None)), cost_usd=charged)
72|            return None
73|        ids = self._charge(trace)
74|        if trace is None:
75|            self.note(action, target, describe(value), ids)
76|        else:
77|            self.note(action, target, describe(value), ids, model_id=trace.model_id,
78|                      input_tokens=trace.input_tokens, output_tokens=trace.output_tokens,
79|                      latency_ms=trace.latency_ms, cost_usd=trace.cost_usd + trace.prior_cost_usd)
80|        return value
81|
82|    def _charge(self, trace: ProviderTrace | None) -> list[str]:
83|        if trace is None:
84|            return []
85|        self.spend_usd += trace.cost_usd + trace.prior_cost_usd
86|        return [trace.call_id, *trace.prior_call_ids]

74|            *(f"finding {f.finding_id}: {r}" for f in self.findings for r in f.visual_evidence
75|              if r not in region_ids),

1|# Data handling for the staged real-media tests (batch 21)
2|
3|Until now, Anamnesis has run only on synthetic media: rendered photos and macOS text-to-speech voices. Batch 21 adds the first real phone photos and a real human voice. This note sets the rules before anything is recorded (supervisor review of 27 Oct, item 9). It covers every photo and voice note used in tests, the demo and the video.
4|
5|## What may be recorded
6|- **Packs.** Real medicine boxes and blister strips, photographed on a plain surface.
7|  - Prefer over-the-counter packs that Ahmed bought himself. Never use a family member's current prescription.
8|  - No pack with a pharmacy dispensing label, unless the label is fully covered with paper before the photo is taken. Covering means covering, not blurring afterwards.
9|- **Voice.** Only Ahmed's own voice, reading a fictional script.
10|  - The patient in the script is invented: the medicines, amounts and history are nobody's real history, Ahmed's included.
11|  - No other voices: no family, no children, no background conversation or TV.
12|- Ahmed records everything on his own phone and consents to sending it to Meta's Model API, as described below.
13|
14|## What must never be in a photo or a recording
15|- Names, addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers, prescription or insurance numbers, pharmacy or prescriber names.
16|- Faces or other people, children, documents, screens, mail, house numbers, or anything that shows where the photo was taken.
17|- Real symptoms or diagnoses of a real person.
18|
19|If something slips in, the file is retaken, never edited afterwards.
20|
21|## Where the files live
22|- **Raw files** go to `evidence/raw/media/real/` on the Pro. That folder is git-ignored: no raw photo or recording is committed, synced to Drive or put in Notion.
23|- **Photos.** Before any model sees a photo, the pipeline turns it upright and strips all its metadata, GPS included (SPEC §4 step 0). Turning off Location for the camera is still recommended. iPhone HEIC files are converted to JPEG locally with `sips`.
24|- **Voice notes** are converted locally to 16 kHz mono WAV with their metadata removed (`ffmpeg -map_metadata -1`), the only format Voice Transcribe accepts. From 28 Oct, `scripts/intake_live.py` also re-writes each WAV to its audio frames alone before any call, so a skipped conversion step can't send a metadata chunk.
25|- **Deletion:** after judging, on Ahmed's word, the raw files move to the Trash.
26|
27|## What leaves the machine
28|- **Only to Meta's Model API**, on Ahmed's account:
29|  - the prepared photo and the crops cut from it, to SAM 3.1 and Muse Spark 1.3;
30|  - the WAV, to Muse Voice Transcribe.
31|- **Standard models only**, never a `*-contributor` id. Meta's pricing page says contributor mode lets Meta train on prompts, files and responses. Our notes (`docs/muse/`) don't record what Meta keeps in standard mode, so anything sent counts as having left our control.
32|- **Public test photos only, for the open-weight comparison (batch 22) and the intake with Spark Open as its label reader (28 Oct, Ahmed's yes):** the Wikimedia Commons and Cairo University CC BY photos may also go to Fireworks or Baseten, to be read by Meta's open-weight Muse Spark Open. `scripts/intake_live.py --reader baseten` and `--reader fireworks` (batch 26) refuse any other photo before the first call. **Ahmed's own photos and voice never go there.**
33|- **The Glimmer fine-tune (29 Oct, Ahmed's call):** the generated fine-tune data (`finetune/data/` and `finetune/data_v2/`, whose Spanish brand names come from AEMPS's public CIMA registry), with the 33 synthetic-voice transcripts of its real slice, may go to Modal, where Meta's open-weight Muse Glimmer is trained and run. Its weights come from the Hugging Face Hub, and nothing goes to the Hub. No photo, no audio and nothing of Ahmed's goes to Modal.
34|- **The second reader (batch 28, 31 Oct, Ahmed's go):** `scripts/intake_live.py --second-reader fireworks` sends Fireworks only the crops of a staged case's public photos that Spark 1.3 couldn't read, even after its zoom. The script refuses any other photo before the first call. **Ahmed's own photos and voice never go there.**
35|- **The tuned extractor on Modal (batch 26, 30 Oct, Ahmed's go):** `scripts/intake_live.py --extractor glimmer` sends the transcript text of a staged case's synthetic voice note (`evidence/raw/media/public/voice/`, macOS `say`) to the tuned Muse Glimmer on Modal. The audio, the photos and anything of Ahmed's never go there: the script refuses any other voice note before the first call.
36|- **Spanish and German synthetic voice notes (batch 24, 29 Oct):** eight macOS `say` notes, in the voices Mónica (es_ES) and Anna (de_DE), read invented scripts (`scripts/make_es_de_media.sh`). They go only to Muse Voice Transcribe on Meta's API, and the four Commons photos used with them go only to SAM 3.1 and Spark 1.3 (`evidence/batches/24/manifest.md`). They serve those runs only: the macOS licence keeps system voices out of the video and any hosted brief.
37|- **The reviewers never see the media.** The batch supervisor (Claude) and the quality manager (Gemini) get code and text evidence only.
38|
39|## What is committed or published
40|- **Committed:**
41|  - the expected results, written down before any model sees a file;
42|  - the transcripts of the fictional scripts;
43|  - each run's findings, cost and latency;
44|  - the summary tables.
45|- **Never committed:** photos, audio, crops, or a clinician brief that embeds them. Briefs stay in `evidence/raw/briefs/`.
46|- **Published only with Ahmed's yes:** a hosted demo brief or video that uses his voice or the real photos needs his explicit yes for that file.
47|
48|## How results are reported
49|- As staged tests with real packaging and a fictional history. They are not a validation, not clinical use, and involve no real patient.
50|- The expected results come first, and every run is reported as it came out (correct, wrong or missed), failures included.
51|- Spend is capped at $1 on the Meta ledger for all staged runs (`SpendGuard`), and each intake has its own session cap.

178|def _find_dose_volumes(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
179|    """Every volume (a number other than 1) and spoon span in the whole text."""
180|    spans = []
181|    for match in _VOLUME_RE.finditer(text):
182|        volume = parse_amount_text(match.group(1))
183|        if volume is not None and volume != 1:
184|            spans.append(match.span())

191|def _skip_fillers(text: str, pos: int) -> int:
192|    """Skip whitespace and bracketed text (brackets aren't counted)."""
193|    while True:
194|        while pos < len(text) and text[pos].isspace():
195|            pos += 1
196|        bracket = _BRACKET_RE.match(text, pos)
197|        if bracket is None:
198|            return pos

202|def _followed_by_water(text: str, start: int, end: int) -> bool:
203|    """True when a water word follows, with only the SPEC's short list between."""
204|    pos = _skip_fillers(text, end)
205|    if pos < len(text) and text[pos] == ")":
206|        opening = text.rfind("(", 0, start)
207|        if opening >= 0 and ")" not in text[opening:start]:
208|            pos = _skip_fillers(text, pos + 1)
209|    link = _DISSOLVE_LINK_RE.match(text, pos)
210|    if link is not None:
211|        pos = _skip_fillers(text, link.end())
212|    while (word := _DISSOLVE_ADJECTIVE_RE.match(text, pos)) is not None:
213|        pos = _skip_fillers(text, word.end())
214|    water = _WATER_RE.match(text, pos)
215|    return water is not None and _WATER_EXCLUSION_RE.match(text, water.end()) is None

218|def _inside_water_brackets(text: str, start: int, end: int) -> bool:
219|    """True for a lone volume in brackets right after a water word."""
220|    if start >= len(text) or not text[start].isdigit():
221|        return False
222|    opening = text.rfind("(", 0, start)
223|    if opening < 0 or ")" in text[opening:start]:
224|        return False
225|    closing = text.find(")", end)
226|    if closing < 0 or "(" in text[end:closing]:
227|        return False
228|    water = _WATER_BEFORE_BRACKET_RE.search(text[:opening])
229|    if water is None or _WATER_EXCLUSION_RE.match(text, water.end()) is not None:
230|        return False
231|    if text[end:closing].strip():
232|        return False
233|    before = text[opening + 1:start].strip()
234|    return not before or _APPROX_RE.fullmatch(before) is not None

279|def _strip_brackets(gap: str) -> str:
280|    """Remove bracketed text, which the before-form does not count."""
281|    for _ in range(3):
282|        stripped = _BRACKET_RE.sub(" ", gap)
283|        stripped = _SQUARE_BRACKET_RE.sub(" ", stripped)
284|        if stripped == gap:

290|def _gap_has_sentence_end(gap: str) -> bool:
291|    """True when the before-form gap crosses a sentence end (SPEC §2)."""
292|    for pos, char in enumerate(gap):
293|        if char in ";!?؛":
294|            return True
295|        if (
296|            char == "."
297|            and _SENTENCE_DOT_RE.match(gap, pos) is not None
298|            and not _is_abbrev_dot(gap, pos)
299|        ):
300|            return True
301|    return False

304|def _printed_before_volume(text: str, number_end: int, volume_start: int) -> bool:
305|    """True when the gap holds up to five words, a connector, an optional each, `(`."""
306|    gap = _strip_brackets(text[number_end:volume_start])
307|    if _gap_has_sentence_end(gap):
308|        return False
309|    if _TABLET_RE.search(gap) is not None:
310|        # A tablet word means dissolving only with `in` or `في`; after `/`,
311|        # `per`, `por`, `par` or `لكل` it excuses nothing (batch 23.1).
312|        return (
313|            _BEFORE_SLASH_RE.match(gap) is not None
314|            or _BEFORE_WORD_PER_RE.match(gap) is not None
315|        )

321|    match = _PER_1ML_RE.match(text, pos)

323|        return True
324|    if per == "dose":

330|def _is_abbrev_dot(text: str, dot_pos: int) -> bool:
331|    """True when the dot follows a word of one to three Latin letters."""
332|    j = dot_pos - 1
333|    n = 0
334|    while j >= 0 and ("A" <= text[j] <= "Z" or "a" <= text[j] <= "z"):
335|        n += 1
336|        j -= 1
337|    return 1 <= n <= 3

340|def _find_sentence_end(text: str, end: int):
341|    """First sentence end after a volume, skipping abbreviation dots."""
342|    tail = text[end:]
343|    for match in _SENTENCE_END_RE.finditer(tail):
344|        if match.group(0) == "." and _is_abbrev_dot(text, end + match.start()):
345|            continue
346|        return match
347|    return None

350|def _printed_beside_a_volume(
351|    text: str, spans: list[tuple[int, int]], amounts: set, per: str
352|) -> bool:
353|    """True when a reading amount is also printed over a volume or after it in its sentence."""
354|    for start, end in spans:
355|        for number in _NUMBER_RE.finditer(text[:start]):
356|            if parse_amount_text(number.group(0)) not in amounts:
357|                continue
358|            if _printed_before_volume(text, number.end(), start):
359|                return True
360|        tail = text[end:]
361|        stop = _find_sentence_end(text, end)
362|        segment = tail[:stop.start()] if stop is not None else tail
363|        for number in _NUMBER_RE.finditer(segment):
364|            amount = parse_amount_text(number.group(0))
365|            if amount not in amounts:
366|                continue
367|            if per in ("ml", "dose") and _starts_own_print(text, end + number.start(), amount, per):
368|                continue
369|            return True
370|    return False

373|def _per_other_volume(label_text: str, strength: dict) -> bool:
374|    """True when a counting volume or spoon drops the strength (SPEC §2)."""
375|    text = label_text.translate(_DIGITS)
376|    amounts = {part["amount"] for part in strength["ingredients"]}
377|    per = str(strength.get("per")).lower()
378|    if per not in ("ml", "dose", "tablet", "capsule"):
379|        return False
380|    spans = _find_dose_volumes(text)
381|    if not any(_counts_as_dose(text, start, end, per) for start, end in spans):
382|        return False
383|    if per in ("tablet", "capsule", "dose"):
384|        for start, _ in spans:
385|            if _AFTER_AMOUNT_RE.search(text[:start]) is not None:
386|                return True
387|    if per == "ml":
388|        printed = all(_printed_per_1ml(text, amount) for amount in amounts)
389|    elif per == "dose":
390|        printed = all(
391|            _printed_per_1ml(text, amount) or _printed_per_dose(text, amount) for amount in amounts
392|        )
393|    else:
394|        printed = all(_printed_per_tablet(text, amount) for amount in amounts)
395|    if not printed:
396|        return True
397|    return _printed_beside_a_volume(text, spans, amounts, per)

363|        for number in _NUMBER_RE.finditer(segment):

1|# Data handling for the staged real-media tests (batch 21)
2|
3|Until now, Anamnesis has run only on synthetic media: rendered photos and macOS text-to-speech voices. Batch 21 adds the first real phone photos and a real human voice. This note sets the rules before anything is recorded (supervisor review of 27 Oct, item 9). It covers every photo and voice note used in tests, the demo and the video.
4|
5|## What may be recorded
6|- **Packs.** Real medicine boxes and blister strips, photographed on a plain surface.
7|  - Prefer over-the-counter packs that Ahmed bought himself. Never use a family member's current prescription.
8|  - No pack with a pharmacy dispensing label, unless the label is fully covered with paper before the photo is taken. Covering means covering, not blurring afterwards.
9|- **Voice.** Only Ahmed's own voice, reading a fictional script.
10|  - The patient in the script is invented: the medicines, amounts and history are nobody's real history, Ahmed's included.
11|  - No other voices: no family, no children, no background conversation or TV.
12|- Ahmed records everything on his own phone and consents to sending it to Meta's Model API, as described below.
13|
14|## What must never be in a photo or a recording
15|- Names, addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers, prescription or insurance numbers, pharmacy or prescriber names.
16|- Faces or other people, children, documents, screens, mail, house numbers, or anything that shows where the photo was taken.
17|- Real symptoms or diagnoses of a real person.
18|
19|If something slips in, the file is retaken, never edited afterwards.
20|
21|## Where the files live
22|- **Raw files** go to `evidence/raw/media/real/` on the Pro. That folder is git-ignored: no raw photo or recording is committed, synced to Drive or put in Notion.
23|- **Photos.** Before any model sees a photo, the pipeline turns it upright and strips all its metadata, GPS included (SPEC §4 step 0). Turning off Location for the camera is still recommended. iPhone HEIC files are converted to JPEG locally with `sips`.
24|- **Voice notes** are converted locally to 16 kHz mono WAV with their metadata removed (`ffmpeg -map_metadata -1`), the only format Voice Transcribe accepts. From 28 Oct, `scripts/intake_live.py` also re-writes each WAV to its audio frames alone before any call, so a skipped conversion step can't send a metadata chunk.
25|- **Deletion:** after judging, on Ahmed's word, the raw files move to the Trash.
26|
27|## What leaves the machine
28|- **Only to Meta's Model API**, on Ahmed's account:
29|  - the prepared photo and the crops cut from it, to SAM 3.1 and Muse Spark 1.3;
30|  - the WAV, to Muse Voice Transcribe.
31|- **Standard models only**, never a `*-contributor` id. Meta's pricing page says contributor mode lets Meta train on prompts, files and responses. Our notes (`docs/muse/`) don't record what Meta keeps in standard mode, so anything sent counts as having left our control.
32|- **Public test photos only, for the open-weight comparison (batch 22) and the intake with Spark Open as its label reader (28 Oct, Ahmed's yes):** the Wikimedia Commons and Cairo University CC BY photos may also go to Fireworks or Baseten, to be read by Meta's open-weight Muse Spark Open. `scripts/intake_live.py --reader baseten` and `--reader fireworks` (batch 26) refuse any other photo before the first call. **Ahmed's own photos and voice never go there.**
33|- **The Glimmer fine-tune (29 Oct, Ahmed's call):** the generated fine-tune data (`finetune/data/` and `finetune/data_v2/`, whose Spanish brand names come from AEMPS's public CIMA registry), with the 33 synthetic-voice transcripts of its real slice, may go to Modal, where Meta's open-weight Muse Glimmer is trained and run. Its weights come from the Hugging Face Hub, and nothing goes to the Hub. No photo, no audio and nothing of Ahmed's goes to Modal.
34|- **The second reader (batch 28, 31 Oct, Ahmed's go):** `scripts/intake_live.py --second-reader fireworks` sends Fireworks only the crops of a staged case's public photos that Spark 1.3 couldn't read, even after its zoom. The script refuses any other photo before the first call. **Ahmed's own photos and voice never go there.**
35|- **The tuned extractor on Modal (batch 26, 30 Oct, Ahmed's go):** `scripts/intake_live.py --extractor glimmer` sends the transcript text of a staged case's synthetic voice note (`evidence/raw/media/public/voice/`, macOS `say`) to the tuned Muse Glimmer on Modal. The audio, the photos and anything of Ahmed's never go there: the script refuses any other voice note before the first call.
36|- **Spanish and German synthetic voice notes (batch 24, 29 Oct):** eight macOS `say` notes, in the voices Mónica (es_ES) and Anna (de_DE), read invented scripts (`scripts/make_es_de_media.sh`). They go only to Muse Voice Transcribe on Meta's API, and the four Commons photos used with them go only to SAM 3.1 and Spark 1.3 (`evidence/batches/24/manifest.md`). They serve those runs only: the macOS licence keeps system voices out of the video and any hosted brief.
37|- **The reviewers never see the media.** The batch supervisor (Claude) and the quality manager (Gemini) get code and text evidence only.
38|
39|## What is committed or published
40|- **Committed:**
41|  - the expected results, written down before any model sees a file;
42|  - the transcripts of the fictional scripts;
43|  - each run's findings, cost and latency;
44|  - the summary tables.
45|- **Never committed:** photos, audio, crops, or a clinician brief that embeds them. Briefs stay in `evidence/raw/briefs/`.
46|- **Published only with Ahmed's yes:** a hosted demo brief or video that uses his voice or the real photos needs his explicit yes for that file.
47|
48|## How results are reported
49|- As staged tests with real packaging and a fictional history. They are not a validation, not clinical use, and involve no real patient.

## 1. Verdict

Build follows SPEC §4 step 5b on the contract's paths, but lets a readable second reading erase first-read evidence the contract never exercises.

## 2. Findings

1. **Severity: medium. Readable second that names nothing replaces a naming first.** Diff `loop.py::_second_read` only conflicts when *both* sides name ingredients (`SPEC.md:353`), and only compares strengths when *both* have one. A `READABLE` second needs only `label_text` ([spark.py](<repo>/.muse/worktrees/20261031-b11a/anamnesis/providers/spark.py:137)), so a second with `inn=None, strength=None` replaces a partial first with `inn`/strength; same for first-with-strength vs second inn-only (amount lost). The pack flips from `unreadable_source` (re-requestable, [review.py](<repo>/.muse/worktrees/20261031-b11a/anamnesis/review.py:37)) to a readable observation with no identity. Contract's readable seconds always name ingredients. Fix: when the first names ingredients and the readable second names none (or drops the strength), keep the first and log `conflict: kept the first reading`.

2. **Severity: low. `per` ignored in agreement, so tablet↔ml swaps replace.** Diff `_strength_key` is `(inn, amount, unit)` only, per `SPEC.md:353`. First partial 250 mg per tablet + second readable 250 mg per ml agree and replace, yet reconciler branches on `per` ([SPEC.md](<repo>/.muse/worktrees/20261031-b11a/SPEC.md:302)). Untested. Fix: include `per` in the key (conflict on differ), or keep first on `per` mismatch.

3. **Severity: low. Conflict/wrong-region logs two `second_read` steps.** `session.call` always notes one step ([session.py](<repo>/.muse/worktrees/20261031-b11a/anamnesis/agent/session.py:77)), then the diff `session.note`s `conflict...` / `error: reading for another region`; SPEC says "a `second_read` step ..." ([SPEC.md](<repo>/.muse/worktrees/20261031-b11a/SPEC.md:352)). Timeline shows a phantom `readable` row; tests only assert `[-1]`. Fix: emit a single step for the rejected second read (zoom has the same shape at [loop.py](<repo>/.muse/worktrees/20261031-b11a/anamnesis/agent/loop.py:114); keep both consistent).

## 3. What you checked and found fine

No-reader path returns early with identical budget/steps; default budgets add `top_k`/photo in loop, re-photo and live script; explicit budget untouched; crop is `crop_region` un-enlarged with `cropped=True`; zoom→second-read stays per-region in order; wrong-region and unreadable/partial seconds keep the first; re-photo supersedes only with ≥1 observation; timeline renders the new action generically; `--second-reader` guards (`--case`, `--reader spark`, public photos) run before any key/client read and reuse the Fireworks wording.
